gap: No result ChatGPT got states, together with a price on a retailer page opened today, that its 'best overall' CyberPower CP1500PFCLCD costs $239.99 at Dell on 2026-11-14 and offers only single-boost AVR (Dell lists an 88–144 V input range, a 4 ms transfer to battery, and 10 minutes of runtime at half load or 2.5 at full). That is the line-interactive 'conditioning' ChatGPT itself said falls short of an online double-conversion UPS.
standout_why: I could not open any rival page. The CyberPower product page (cyberpowersystems.com, result 1) returned 405, B&H's compare page and Micro Center returned 403, the Eaton SMART1500LCDT page timed out twice, and the two SMT1500C PDFs and the Newegg CP1500PFCLCD datasheet PDF would not extract. CyberPower's own page and datasheets are in ChatGPT's results and probably list the AVR type, input range and transfer time, so the spec half is likely already there. What looks new is the price on a retailer page read today ($239.99 at Dell, against the $239.95 Newegg figure ChatGPT showed). The other new piece would be a sourced price for an online double-conversion unit, which ChatGPT mentioned without naming a model or price. I could not source that piece.
decides: This confirms the CP1500PFCLCD as the low-cost pick at about $240 with sine-wave output, but its conditioning is single-boost AVR with a 4 ms transfer, not regenerated power. A shopper who needs real power conditioning has to move up to an online double-conversion UPS. I could not get an opened price for one (CyberPower OL1500RTXL2U), so the page cannot yet put a number on that step.
